name: Pulse — Neural Feed Network
description: Pulse is the dominant BCI-direct social network in GLMZ, allowing users to broadcast compressed emotional states, sensory snippets, and curated memory fragments to followers in real time. Founded in 2201 by Yemisi Okafor-Brandt and the ELF collective known as Threefold, Pulse operates on a tiered bandwidth model — Tier 1-2 users get lossy 'ghost feeds' while Tier 4-5 subscribers experience full-fidelity neural streams. Content on Pulse is ephemeral by default, dissolving after 48 hours unless 'crystallized' by paying a preservation fee. The platform is technically universal but its premium experience is aggressively paywalled, making the Shelf community's stripped-down version — called the Hollow — feel like a different network entirely.
cultural_impact: Pulse has fundamentally altered how GLMZ residents process and perform emotion — the concept of 'feeding a moment' has entered daily vocabulary, and psychiatric clinics report a new disorder called Feed Dysmorphia, where users struggle to experience life without simultaneously broadcasting it.
locations: The Hollow node cluster, Shelf Ward 7
Threefold server sanctuary, undisclosed Tier 3 basement
story_hooks: A Shelf kid's raw, unfiltered grief feed goes viral on Tier 4-5 Pulse, attracting corporate attention that could lift her out of Ward 7 — or exploit her trauma for profit
A crystallized memory from a murdered corponation whistleblower surfaces on Pulse four years after their death, and someone is paying heavily to have it scrubbed before it dissolves
Threefold begins broadcasting fragments of a future-tense memory feed that shouldn't be possible — and the content accurately predicts three deaths before anyone takes it seriously
user_base: Approximately 4.2 million active users; heaviest concentration in Tier 2-3 working population aged 16-40
monetization: Tiered subscription bandwidth, memory crystallization fees, emotional targeting advertising sold to corponations, premium follower analytics
notable_feature: Ghost Feeds — the degraded Tier 1-2 broadcast format has developed its own aesthetic language, with deliberate signal noise and compression artifacts adopted as artistic style by Shelf creators
